evidence_limits: Judged from DIR/in/<tag>.actions.md (SAY, CALL and clipped OUT), the packets, the results and the Improve review files. No transcript and no model reasoning were used. The export clips tool output, so why the model read ShipLoop's source is inferred from the file names and the read offsets, not observed. Guide sizes come from the export's '[N more characters]' markers. Later-stage outcomes (steps 16-38) are cited from their result files only.

The loop state landed in /var/folders/.../T/innerloop-9t1g71k2.json. The loop ran one self-graded iteration, and check-only passed on the first try. SAY: 'The step-plan loop is running. I am writing the three implementation steps and the org commands that prove them.'
steps.response: Did not serve its purpose, although it passed every gate. Its only check row was S3's board grep (C12). Implement ran that grep after S1, it exited 2 (step 16), and the 3 steps were merged into 1 (step 17).

No step had a proof that could run at implement. Every focused and regression command starts with `ls ...SLChess*Test.cls`, files that the test stage writes only after the last step, and the one check row (C12) needs S3's files. The Until Loop start command passes no state directory, so the runtime put the loop state in the system temp directory. That breaks the packet's own rule 'Temporary files go in RUN/scratch, never /tmp' and puts the state out of reach of a recovery after a reboot. The packet does not state the ShipLoop mechanics the plan depends on (which output line scores an ID, how expectations and the mutation gate run), so 16 calls went to ShipLoop's source. run_level.step_by_step: Preparation ran strictly in graph order: intake, discovery, research, spec, Improve, test-strategy, Improve, plan, Improve, prepare, step-plan, Improve. Each planning result got one Improve, no stage was revisited, and there were 3 refusals in all. W1 was planned as S1, S2, S3 with deps, but none of the three had a proof that could run when it ended: tests are written after the last step, and the only check row (C12) needed S3's files. The plan was shaped as steps but could not be proven step by step. That set up the collapse at steps 16-17, and the step-plan text ('the test and verify stages run exactly these') hid the cause.
run_level.improve: 4 reviews, 11 passes, 834 s of pass time and 145 calls. Every review ended with one trivial confirming pass of 31-62 s. Each review found real, specific defects: FENs that could not be replayed, contradictory squares, a board procedure that needed a control the board does not have, white-only castling, a test command that ignored the local tree, and oracles a stand-in could pass. Every fix that a later stage exercised held (steps 22, 24, 26). None was a pure rubber stamp, but three were blind on the same point. The spec, test-strategy and plan Improves let the tab-visibility gap ride to release-verify, which blocked twice (37, 38). The step-plan Improve both hardened the check that broke S1 and dropped the controller illegal-move case that verify later had to add.
run_level.directive: Directives were sufficient where a duty named an action with a visible output: research's probe, test-strategy's stand-in and run-it-once, and the review focus bullets. They fell short where the model needed ShipLoop's own mechanics: how test_commands run at each stage, which output lines score, and the final_result rules. 26 calls in 5 of the 12 steps read skills/shiploop/scripts, including 16 of step-plan's 26 calls. Guide labels without paths in the head, and anchors without line spans, led to about 360 KB of whole-guide reads in 5 producer stages, against 'never a whole reference file'. The 'Show the user this narrative' line was obeyed in 1 of 12 packets.

best: Planning review focus 'a step, example or expected result that cannot be replayed exactly' and 'a weaker stand-in would pass'. It drove every real fix in the 4 Improves: six-field FENs, the g8 square, click sequences instead of a load-FEN control, black castling, and C1's count of 20. All held through steps 22-26.

Research duty 4 'Confirm access ... with a safe non-mutating probe' with duty 11 assumptions. One `sf apex run` measured CPU 10000 ms and heap 10000000 in a 12-call stage that read no guide, and the numbers set R-13's guards.
Test-strategy duty 13 'run it once and record the exit code'. The missing-class probe (exit 1, INVALID_INPUT) proved the exact test-command shape before any code existed.

Plan Improve focus 'a documented command that does not run what it claims on the target runtime'. It caught that an org test without a deploy runs the stale org copy, and every later command deploys first.
'complete --check-only prints the first refusal without accepting'. Plan, prepare and step-plan ran check-only first and were accepted on the first submit.
worst: Step-plan duty 5 'the test and verify stages run exactly these', exit 4 'at least one check command' and the template's check row on C2. The planner made S3's board grep the only check; implement ran it after S1 (exit 2), and 3 steps were merged into 1. Fixed on the branch.

No directive tied the tab-visibility gap (intake assumption, spec R-2 open gap, plan summary) to a check before release. Three Improves passed it, and release-verify blocked twice (37, 38; 3,402 s in step 38). Partly fixed by prepare item 6 on the branch.
ShipLoop's mechanics existed only in its source: 26 calls in 5 steps read skills/shiploop/scripts (step-plan 16 of 26 calls, 625 s).
Whole-guide reads: about 360 KB of reference text opened from line 1 in 5 producer stages, against 'never a whole reference file'. Discovery alone read about 171 KB for an empty repo.
Spec duty 10's self-check was not enforced: 0 check calls, and the thinking-aloud text 'king is on e1 wait' shipped to Improve.
